bib.title: Chapter 5: Monte Carlo Methods (Reinforcement Learning: An Introduction, 2nd ed.)

question: How can value functions and optimal policies be learned from sampled episodes alone, without a model of the environment?
contributions: MC control with exploring starts, on-policy epsilon-soft, and off-policy via importance sampling

limits: Monte Carlo defined only for episodic tasks; updates only after episode ends.
Convergence of Monte Carlo ES is not formally proved; authors call it one of the most fundamental open theoretical questions in RL.
Off-policy MC for prediction and control remains unsettled; insufficient experience to assess slow learning from episode tails.
Discounting-aware and per-decision IS are described as cutting-edge research; no consistent per-decision weighted estimator is known.
Only blackjack and a 1-state MDP are run; racetrack is an unsolved exercise.
practices: Estimate action values rather than state values when no model is available (Sec 5.2).
Use weighted importance sampling in practice; keep ordinary IS for easier extension to function approximation (Sec 5.5).
Use every-visit MC in practice for ease of extension to approximation (Sec 5.5).
Use an incremental mean/weighted-mean update (counts C) rather than storing return lists (Sec 5.6, Ex 5.4).
Make the behavior policy soft (epsilon-soft) so every action is tried infinitely often (Sec 5.7).

On-policy methods attempt to evaluate or improve the policy that is used to make decisions, whereas off-policy methods evaluate or improve a policy different from that used to generate the data
pi(a|s) >= epsilon/|A(s)| for all states and actions, for some epsilon > 0
relative probability of the trajectory under target and behavior policies: product of pi(Ak|Sk)/b(Ak|Sk)
weighted average of returns, sum(rho G)/sum(rho), zero if denominator is zero (5.6)
G-bar_{t:h} = R_{t+1}+...+R_h, undiscounted, stopping at horizon h
scale each reward only by the ratio up to its own time step, G-tilde_t

code.snippet: Loop forever (for each episode): choose S0,A0 randomly, all pairs prob > 0; generate episode from S0,A0 following pi; G <- 0; for t=T-1..0: G <- gamma*G + R_{t+1}; unless (St,At) appears earlier: Append G to Returns(St,At); Q(St,At) <- average(Returns(St,At)); pi(St) <- argmax_a Q(St,a)

code.where: p.110 box, off-policy MC prediction (weighted IS, incremental)
code.snippet: G <- 0; W <- 1; for t=T-1..0 while W != 0: G <- gamma*G + R_{t+1}; C(St,At) <- C(St,At) + W; Q(St,At) <- Q(St,At) + W/C(St,At) [G - Q(St,At)]; W <- W * pi(At|St)/b(At|St)
... pi(St) <- argmax_a Q(St,a); If At != pi(St) then exit inner Loop; W <- W * 1/b(At|St)
